citation: Terms of Service and DPA; two negotiated DPAs (contract)

deadline: Without undue delay and within 72 hours of confirmation; 48 hours for the 2 negotiated DPAs (salon group and grooming franchise group)
notify: Each affected subscriber's account owner or security contact

obligation: Florida third-party agent notice to the covered entity
trigger: Breach of security of a system the company maintains for subscribers, involving personal information of Florida residents as defined in 501.171(1)(g)
deadline: As expeditiously as practicable, but no later than 10 days following the determination of the breach or reason to believe the breach occurred. Give each subscriber all information it needs for its own notices
notify: Each affected subscriber (the covered entity), which then gives notice under 501.171(3) and (4)
applies_at_this_tier: Yes if Florida personal information is involved (about 61,000 Florida end clients). Counsel decides whether the data elements qualify: names with phone, email, and appointment history alone are not listed elements; free-text service notes that describe a physical condition, and home addresses, need counsel's view

obligation: Florida breach notice to individuals (company-owned data)
trigger: Breach of personal information the company owns, mainly subscriber staff sign-in emails with passwords, where the passwords are not secured (501.171(1)(g)1.b. and 2.)
deadline: As expeditiously as practicable, no later than 30 days after determination of the breach or reason to believe it occurred. Not required if, after investigation and consultation with law enforcement, the company reasonably determines in writing that identity theft or other financial harm is not likely; keep that determination 5 years and send it to the Department of Legal Affairs within 30 days (501.171(4)(c))
applies_at_this_tier: Only for company-owned data. Counsel decides whether salted, hashed passwords are secured and therefore excluded. Forced password resets are done either way

obligation: Florida notice to the Department of Legal Affairs
trigger: Breach affecting 500 or more individuals in Florida, where the company is the covered entity
deadline: As expeditiously as practicable, no later than 30 days after determination (15 more days for notice to individuals, not for this notice, if good cause is given in writing within the 30 days)
notify: Florida Department of Legal Affairs (Attorney General)
applies_at_this_tier: Only as covered entity and 500 or more Florida individuals (about 520 subscriber staff accounts in total, so possible only if most are Florida residents)

obligation: Florida notice to consumer reporting agencies
trigger: Notice required to more than 1,000 individuals at a single time
notify: All nationwide consumer reporting agencies (timing, distribution, and content of the notices)
applies_at_this_tier: Unlikely as covered entity (about 520 subscriber staff accounts); subscribers decide for their own notices

citation: State breach notification statutes (all 50 states, DC, PR, USVI; Guam 9 GCA Ch. 48)
trigger: Breach of computerized personal information of residents of other states (definitions vary by state)
deadline: Varies by state (for example "without unreasonable delay" or a fixed number of days); many states also require a service provider to tell the data owner
notify: Data owners (subscribers) and, for company-owned data, affected residents and any regulator the state requires
applies_at_this_tier: Always check. Apply the law of each state where affected individuals reside (subscribers in 11 states). Counsel checks each state's definition against the data taken
